title: Chapter 79: A Chance to Redeem Yourself
html:
A strange odor filled the cramped girls’ room. Beyond the flashlight’s beam, a bedsheet stirred as though something were crawling out from beneath it. Rain tapped against the window. A storm raged outside, yet the dormitory was eerily silent.

With his arm suspended over the white paper, Chen Ge tried to relax. After chanting the invocation, he felt a distinct pressure on the back of his hand, as though someone had laid their hand over his. Cold seeped from unseen fingertips.

“Pen Spirit, Pen Spirit, you are my spirit from my previous life, and I am your spirit in this life. If you are with us, please draw a circle on the paper.”

Chen Ge chanted again, and the cold on the back of his hand intensified. Yet to his confusion, the pen remained upright and motionless. It did not draw a circle; it did nothing at all.

The Pen Spirit refuses to answer my call?

Pressure thickened the air as the chill spread from the back of his hand up his arm.

For some reason, I feel like a few more individuals have joined me in this room.

Chen Ge focused, his pupils widening in the dark. Through his Yin Yang Vision, he made out three blurred shadows standing around him, each reaching for the pen in his hand.

Three of you?

His heart skipped a beat. He blinked, and the image vanished, but that did not mean the shadows had left. His hand felt submerged in ice water. He was certain at least three other hands now gripped the pen with him.

Three ‘individuals’ answered my call. Is this the effect of my ‘Specter’s Favored’ title?

As Chen Ge searched for an answer, the pen hovering over the paper twitched. The movement was slight, but unmistakable.

Is it beginning?

The flashlight beside him dimmed. Under his intent gaze, the pen moved. Its tip dragged across the paper, scratching out a red circle.

Chen Ge knew he had not moved, yet a circle now marked the paper. As he stared at it, he remembered the side mission’s name—The Pen Spirit Who Refused to Leave.

There are three taboos to the Pen Spirit game. One, you mustn’t ask about your cause of death; two, you mustn’t ask about your life expectancy; three, you have to unbind the spirit when you’re done. Violating any one of these will lead to horrible consequences.

The third taboo was the gravest. If not released, the spirit would remain with its summoner until it turned malevolent and killed every player.

“Hopefully nothing goes wrong,” Chen Ge murmured, returning his attention to the white paper. The red circle sat directly in its center.

It heard me. Time to ask some questions.

Chen Ge was there only to complete the black phone’s mission. He had no intention of doing anything foolish enough to anger the spirit.

It’s not every day I summon the Pen Spirit.After some thought, Chen Ge asked the question whose answer he wanted most. “Pen Spirit, Pen Spirit, do you know where my parents are?”

During the bathtub Nightmare Mission, Chen Ge had wanted above all to see his parents, but his wish had gone unfulfilled. At least that suggested they were still alive—missing, not dead.

He genuinely wanted an answer. The pen trembled the moment he asked, and a hairline crack appeared along its barrel.

This was not what he had expected. Is the question really that difficult?

Two minutes later, the room seemed inexplicably brighter. The pen moved again and drew a second circle.

What does that mean? Pass?Studying the two circles, Chen Ge could almost sense the Pen Spirit’s embarrassment. It did not know the answer either.

Strange. My parents’ disappearance must be more complicated than it seems.Chen Ge fell silent. Nothing else inspired the same curiosity. Fine. I’ll ask something random and finish the side mission.

The chill had reached his shoulder. As the game continued, half his body went numb, slowly slipping beyond his control.

“Then I’ll ask something else. Pen Spirit, Pen Spirit, can you tell me who my future wife will be?”

The pen quivered, and the flashlight flickered as though heralding something’s arrival. Tension returned to the room. The window rattled on its hinges as rain seeped inside. Lightning split the sky, and for an instant four shadows appeared on the wall.

His hand weakened as the pen moved. Blood-red strokes appeared on the paper, gradually forming the first character.

“Xu? Is it Xu Wan?” Despite asking on a whim, Chen Ge found his interest piqued. The pen continued moving, but stopped just as it began the second character.

“What’s going on?”

Chen Ge was only a spectator. He exerted no force, yet the pen shook violently in his grip as fresh cracks spread across its surface.

BANG!

Invisible forces seemed to clash within the dark bedroom. The ballpoint pen finally cracked under the strain, and one force appeared to yield. Then Chen Ge saw something astonishing.

The pen in his grasp crossed out the “Xu” that was already written and wrote down another name beside it!

“Zhang… Ya?”

The name stood so crisp and perfect on the paper that Chen Ge did not know how to respond. “Pen Spirit, are you sure that’s the name you meant to write from the beginning?”

No answer came, and the chill vanished from his arm. “Pen Spirit, are you still here? If you can hear me, please draw a circle.”

The Yin energy dissipated completely, and the room returned to normal. The Pen Spirit seemed to have departed without saying goodbye. To be safe, Chen Ge chanted, “Pen Spirit, Pen Spirit, you are my spirit from my previous life, and I am your spirit in this life. If you wish to go, then please go.”

With the game over, Chen Ge stood. The moment he released the ballpoint pen, it split into several pieces. It made a pitiful sight.

My game of Pen Spirit sure is different from others’.

Chen Ge picked up his phone and realized with a start that his livestream’s popularity had surpassed 20,000 views—this was a brand-new record for him.
